lead.headline: Trump tells U.N. he could 'annihilate' Iran as envoys open talks
lead.dek: Witkoff and Kushner held about three hours of mediated talks Tuesday; Iran's president arrived to speak Wednesday
body: President Trump told the U.N. General Assembly on Tuesday that he must decide whether to make a deal with Iran or 'annihilate the Islamic Republic,' hours before his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held about three hours of mediated talks with Iranian negotiators on the sidelines of the assembly in New York.

'Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival?' Trump said, adding that he expected a deal 'right after the election.' Witkoff said the negotiators 'completed a round of discussions that we hope will prove constructive,' with Qatar and Pakistan mediating, Al Jazeera reported. Iran's conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz include an end to the naval blockade and freeing frozen funds, CBS News reported.

Iran's armed forces said the threat showed 'strategic weakness' and warned of 'more severe, crushing, and unpredictable blows,' Al Jazeera reported. President Masoud Pezeshkian arrived in New York late Tuesday to address the assembly Wednesday, the highest-ranking Iranian official on U.S. soil since the war began Feb. 28. Trump said he expects a second round of talks 'in the very near future.'

briefs.headline: DOJ calls White House access a 'privilege' ahead of press-ban hearing
briefs.summary: The Justice Department said in a filing late Tuesday that access is a privilege, not a right, and accused CNN, MS NOW and Politico of publishing classified material. Judge Timothy Kelly hears their restraining-order bid Wednesday.

briefs.headline: U.S. sets aside 17,500 refugee slots mainly for Afrikaners
briefs.summary: The administration told Congress Tuesday that fiscal 2027's 17,500 refugee admissions will go 'primarily' to white South Africans at a projected $500 million, while the program stays closed to most other groups.

briefs.headline: Diesel hits record $6.52 as oil swings on Trump's Iran remarks
briefs.summary: Brent dipped below $98 before the speech, rose when Trump said a deal would wait until after the election, then fell about 1% on word of the talks. Gasoline averages $4.47, up 50% since the war began.

briefs.headline: FBI investigates possible breach of its job application site
briefs.summary: The bureau said it is investigating 'claims regarding unauthorized activity' on FBIjobs.gov, its hiring portal since 2017. ABC News reported, citing sources, that the scope of any exposed data is still being assessed.

briefs.headline: Polo peaks at 175 mph then eases to Category 4 off Mexico
briefs.summary: The NHC said Polo hit 175 mph Tuesday evening and had 155 mph winds at 3 a.m. Wednesday 185 miles south of Zihuatanejo; the core is forecast to stay offshore.

briefs.headline: Kiir dissolves South Sudan government before December vote
briefs.summary: President Salva Kiir's decree Tuesday removed vice presidents, ministers and both assemblies ahead of a Dec. 22 vote, the country's first national election.

briefs.headline: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over 2019 Easter bombings
briefs.summary: A three-judge High Court bench found 14 men guilty on all charges Tuesday and a 15th on some, acquitting nine, after a five-year trial; the attacks killed 279.

briefs.headline: Zelenskyy offers Russia an energy ceasefire after Trump talks
briefs.summary: After meeting Trump at the UN Tuesday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine will stop refinery strikes only if Russia stops hitting its energy system; Trump made no Patriot pledge.

briefs.headline: Crane malfunction kills worker at I-79 bridge site
briefs.summary: A crane sent concrete barriers into three workers on the I-79 bridge at the Marion-Monongalia line Tuesday, State Police said; Mickey Swisher, 30, died and two were hospitalized.

briefs.headline: Mullican Flooring to close Ronceverte plant, cutting 70 jobs
briefs.summary: The Greenbrier County hardwood plant issued 60-day WARN notices Monday and will shut around Thanksgiving, citing weak demand, high inventory and flood-plain insurance and water costs.

briefs.headline: Justices weigh Democrats' challenge to vacated House seat
briefs.summary: Justices heard Tuesday whether the House lawfully vacated Joseph de Soto's Berkeley seat after his 2024 arrest; Chief Justice Haley Bunn asked whether the case is moot with an election weeks away.

briefs.headline: State school board tells justices rule-review law is a veto
briefs.summary: The Board of Education argued Tuesday that HB 2755, which lets lawmakers block its rules, violates a 1988 precedent; the secretary of state's lawyer said rules take effect if the Legislature does nothing.

regional.item: Police said Tuesday they had charged Chase Misner, 20, with malicious assault and wanton endangerment in a Sept. 17 shooting on 31st Street.
A Richmond Elementary aide, 58, and a Dunbar Middle sixth-grader, 12, died in separate South Charleston crashes hours apart Monday.
A vehicle hit a guardrail on Route 50 eastbound near River Hill Road Tuesday afternoon, closing two lanes until 5:44 p.m.
A county grand jury indicted a Pipestem man, 30, on 21 sexual abuse, privacy and strangulation counts, the Hinton News reported Tuesday.

away.item: The county regional commission adopted an Act 181 plan Sept. 17 that lets projects of 50 or fewer homes in North Bennington skip Act 250.

hotspots.item: A Woo-Hoo LLC representative told the county commission Sept. 16 he was prepared to sue over a roughly $160,000 property tax dispute, the Echo reported Monday.
Monday's Pender commission meeting collapsed without a quorum when two of four members stayed away, delaying four public hearings and a $1.2M water contract.

briefs.headline: RCMP link 4 armed robberies of PG vape and cannabis stores
briefs.summary: Prince George RCMP said Tuesday about four masked suspects hit stores on Massey, Westwood and Strathcona between Sept. 6 and 19, bear-spraying staff and taking product and cash. No arrests.

briefs.headline: PG civic candidates say snap vote will drown out local race
briefs.summary: Council hopeful Ron Polillo and former MLA Pat Bell told CKPG Tuesday the Oct. 24 provincial vote, a week after the Oct. 17 civic election with nine mayoral and 18 council candidates, will cut turnout.

briefs.headline: Eby calls snap B.C. election for Oct. 24 citing Trump
briefs.summary: The NDP leader dissolved his majority Tuesday, two years into his mandate, calling U.S. tariffs an 'existential' threat; interim Conservative leader Lorne Doerkson put the cost at $83M to $84M.

briefs.headline: Squamish council rejects $142M Woodfibre LNG tax deal
briefs.summary: Council voted 5-2 Tuesday against a 10-year payment and tax-exemption agreement that would have begun in 2027 and settled three company lawsuits; Coun. Jenna Stoner said payments were not indexed to inflation.

briefs.headline: Belleville synagogue shooting suspect dies in hospital
briefs.summary: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit said Tuesday Sean Ward, 29, died Monday night in Kingston; Const. Jeff Smith is stable in intensive care. National Defence said Ward was an infantry corporal released in 2022.

briefs.headline: Carney defends C-39 strike clause as unions push back
briefs.summary: Carney said Tuesday the bill 'reinforces the right to strike' though it lets the labour minister end stoppages that harm the 'national interest'; CLC president Bea Bruske said a right you cannot exercise is not a right.

briefs.headline: Review finds no causal acetaminophen link to autism, ADHD
briefs.summary: Seven meta-analyses covering more than 3 million participants show the apparent link fading as study quality improves, a Santiago de Compostela-led team said in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology.

briefs.headline: Heat wave seasons ran 39 days longer by 2023, study finds
briefs.summary: First heat waves arrived 3.29 days earlier per decade and the last ended 5.41 days later over 1979-2023, a Chinese Academy of Sciences team said in Nature Climate Change.

briefs.headline: NASA sets Oct. 1 liftoff target for SpaceX Crew-13
briefs.summary: NASA and SpaceX are targeting 11:10 a.m. EDT Oct. 1 from Cape Canaveral, with docking about 8 p.m. the same day; the four-person crew flies to Kennedy on Sept. 26 after an oxidizer leak delayed the mission.

briefs.headline: Olive ridley turtle nests in California, a West Coast first
briefs.summary: NOAA Fisheries documented nests at Seal Beach and Huntington Beach, its first recorded sea turtle nesting on the West Coast; the endangered species' eggs incubate 45 to 60 days, NOAA's Justin Viezbicke said.

briefs.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI release cheaper models hours apart
briefs.summary: Anthropic said Opus 5.5 matches its Fable model on most tasks at a 20% lower price; OpenAI said GPT-6 Sol and Luna handle tasks better than Anthropic's top models. Both claims are the companies' own.

briefs.headline: Meta routes Muse agent calls to human call center workers
briefs.summary: 404 Media reported, citing internal Meta communications, that Muse hands call requests to trained human agents during testing; Meta said the feature will ship only with proper disclosures.

briefs.headline: Triage algorithm could cut FDA device recalls by a third
briefs.summary: A tool that triages 510(k) submissions by predicate-device history would cut review workload 40.5% and improve the recall rate 32.9%, Indiana University and Harvard researchers said in Management Science.

weather_ear: Wednesday's forecast is Jim Claudtore's, at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line; Pezeshkian addresses the U.N. today, Kelly hears the press-ban suit, and Devine is arraigned in Monongalia County.
